name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,585

clue.text: Some Russian music fan, insane, completely losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word for completely is dropped

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a football nut
crackers is informal British for mad
quite in its sense of entirely

explanation.surface: A music fan from Russia has gone utterly mad.
explanation.walkthrough: QUITE minus its Q leaves UITE, which completes NUTCRACKERS UITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's ballet suite is a well-known piece of Russian orchestral composition, so it is an example of such work.

clue.text: Counselling had with husband leaving bad habit

indicators.note: the husband leaving means his letter departs from the word it sits in

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
a vice is a bad habit

explanation.surface: Someone got therapy once their husband walked out over a bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Counselling as a noun is guidance offered to someone, which is a synonym for recommendations given.

clue.text: Coded text in tomb upset woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the name is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a crypt is an underground burial chamber
a woman's name

explanation.surface: An inscription in a grave unsettles a woman visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Any woman's name is fair game in crosswords; here it is MARGO, which turned over gives OGRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptogram is a message written in cipher, so it is a synonym for writing that has been encrypted.

clue.text: Cheap containers

blocks.note: first meaning: shoddy, of little worth
second meaning: read as two words, a tin and a pot, both vessels

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cut-price boxes; the answer split in two names a pair of vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot is an adjective for something inferior or second-rate, while its two halves are each a kind of receptacle.

clue.text: Sea eagle gets between horses in coastal town

indicators.note: getting between means sitting inside, flanked on each side by the other letters

blocks.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle
a bay is a reddish-brown horse

explanation.surface: A sea eagle lands among horses in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horses' supplies two pieces: H (horse being slang for heroin) and BAY. Herne Bay is a seaside resort on the north Kent coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Herne Bay is a resort on the Kent shoreline in England, so it is an example of a seaside settlement.

clue.text: Travel always upset canvasser

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word for always reads bottom to top

blocks.note: to go is to travel
ay (or aye) is an old word meaning always, ever

explanation.surface: A political canvasser is fed up with constantly being on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvasser' looks like a door-to-door campaigner; it is someone who works on canvas, a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya, the Spanish master, painted on canvas, so he is a whimsical example of a painter.

clue.text: Settler: one individual held in veneration

blocks.note: the punctuation mark itself is called a colon
the Roman numeral for one
a saint, abbreviated St, is a person venerated

explanation.surface: A settler is described as someone revered.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon after 'Settler' looks like plain punctuation, but it is part of the wordplay and supplies its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist is someone who goes to live in a new territory, so the word is a synonym for a pioneer inhabitant.

clue.text: Specifically what makes blood thicker than water?

definitions.text: Specifically what makes blood thicker than water?

blocks.clueFragment: Specifically what makes blood thicker than water?
blocks.note: surface reading: the proverb that family ties count for more than other bonds

blocks.clueFragment: Specifically what makes blood thicker than water?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the physics term for how heavy a liquid is compared with water, read with a pun on family members

explanation.walkthrough: 'Specifically' hints at specific gravity, the older name for the same physical measure; the first word of the answer also means family members.
explanation.definitionFit: The physics term compares a substance's mass per volume against water, which is literally what makes blood measurably thicker.

clue.text: Oppressed by false story about new mark

indicators.note: about means going around, so the falsehood surrounds the letter for new

blocks.note: under in the sense of being subjugated
a lie is an untrue account
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone is weighed down by a fabricated tale about a new mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline is to emphasise text by drawing a stroke beneath it, so it is a verb synonym for marking.

clue.text: Wizard seen here complete in fresh and bracing sea air

blocks.note: the land of Oz is where the Wizard of Oz is found
one in the sense of whole, entire

explanation.surface: A wizard is spotted at the seaside taking in the bracing air.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is used informally for the invigorating air at the seaside, a popular sense rather than the chemical one.

clue.text: Pipe radius used in Shard

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, so one letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: a chip is a small broken fragment
R is the standard abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: A pipe's radius is measured for use in the Shard, London's tallest skyscraper.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S on 'Shard' points to the London tower; lower-case it is just a fragment. 'Pipe' is a verb here, a bird's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe is to make a high shrill sound like a bird, which is a synonym for the short twittering call of small birds.

clue.text: No place as rowdy as Floridian location

indicators.note: rowdy means disorderly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Nowhere is quite as rowdy as a particular spot in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensacola is a city in the Florida panhandle on the Gulf coast, so it is an example of a place in that state.

clue.text: Guinness for one presented by east German plant

blocks.note: Sir Alec Guinness, the actor, is an example of an Alec
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: A pint of the Irish stout is offered alongside a plant from eastern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guinness' wants to be a stout and hence ALE, which leaves COST unexplained; it is the actor Alec Guinness.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecost, also called costmary, is an aromatic herb once used to flavour beer, so it is an example of a garden herb.

clue.text: Opera composer uses percussion instrument in one

blocks.note: a bell is struck to make its sound
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A composer of operas includes a percussion part in a single piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is simply taken as written between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincenzo Bellini wrote Norma and La Sonnambula, so he is an example of an Italian writer of operas.

clue.text: Room for experimentation in political choice?

blocks.note: Lab is short for the British Labour Party
or is the word that offers an alternative
a Tory, a member of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A room for trying things out as a political decision.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'Lab or a Tory?', the choice a British voter faces between Labour and the Conservatives; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a workroom equipped for scientific tests, so it is a synonym for a place where research is carried out.

clue.text: Old Cambodian king with me featured in 60 Minutes

indicators.note: featured in means appearing inside, so one piece is set within another

blocks.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
sixty minutes is an hour, abbreviated HR
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old Cambodian king appears alongside the speaker on the American TV news programme 60 Minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Khmer are the people of the ancient empire based at Angkor, so the word names a member of that historic Cambodian civilisation.

clue.text: Tricky fellow's raving maniac imprisoning soldier

indicators.note: raving means wildly out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order
imprisoning means locking up inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A devious man is a raving lunatic who has locked up a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician performs illusions and sleight of hand, so a man who does tricks for an audience fits the description.

clue.text: Place with yard to keep supplying

blocks.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A spot with a yard where provisions are kept flowing.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply someone with drink or food is to offer it repeatedly, a verb idiom for continually providing.

clue.text: Figure given by Defense Department

blocks.note: first meaning: a five-sided geometric shape
second meaning: the US Department of Defense, named after its five-sided headquarters

explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling 'Defense' points to the US. 'Figure' looks like a number, but it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagon is a five-sided plane shape, and the American military headquarters building is named after it.

clue.text: Maybe goat without tail comes to steep-sided hill

indicators.note: without its tail means the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a goat is an example of an animal that butts with its head

explanation.surface: A goat, perhaps missing its tail, arrives at a steep hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' tells you the goat is only one example of a creature that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A butte is an isolated flat-topped hill with sheer flanks, typical of the American West, so it fits that description.

clue.text: Diet has military group shedding tons

indicators.note: shedding means casting off, so a letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: a regiment is an army unit
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: An army unit on a diet loses a great deal of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed programme of food and exercise, so it is a synonym for an eating plan followed for health.

clue.text: Say Bovary at this point hosting love-in

indicators.note: hosting means taking in a guest, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: here means at this place or moment
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Emma Bovary, the adulterous wife of Flaubert's novel, is at this moment holding a love-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma Bovary is the central female character of Flaubert's novel, so she is an example of a leading lady in fiction.

clue.text: Frank does cutting-edge work over time

blocks.note: to hone is to sharpen a blade
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank does pioneering work over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting-edge' suggests innovation; literally it is working on a blade's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank as an adjective means candid and straightforward, a synonym for truthful and sincere.

clue.text: Article to accompany one-on-one in Ancient Greek

blocks.note: one is I, so one on one is I, ON, I
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news article covers a private one-to-one session conducted in Ancient Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to accompany' places the article after the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionians were one of the main tribal groups of classical Hellas, so the word names a member of that early people.

clue.text: Centaur moving home is in two minds

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A centaur can't decide whether to move house.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in two minds is an idiom for wavering between options, so it describes someone unsure or doubtful.

clue.text: Whirl about a bit more elegantly

indicators.note: a bit means a small piece, so the answer is a fragment of the following words

blocks.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone spins around a little more gracefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to spin or lurch round and round, so it is a verb synonym for twirling or spinning.

clue.text: African location where enthusiast returning lives

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for enthusiast is read backwards

blocks.note: a nut is a fan
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A place in Africa where a returning fan has settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia on the Mediterranean, so it is an example of a North African city.

clue.text: Missile guided back to English business

indicators.note: guided back means sent in the opposite direction, so the word reads right to left

blocks.note: a dart is a small thrown missile
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A guided missile is sent back to English commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade means commerce, the buying and selling of goods, so it is a synonym for commercial activity.

clue.text: Keen-eyed ancillary on Russian river

indicators.note: in this across clue, one thing on another means it is placed after it, so the helper follows the river

blocks.note: the Ob is a major river in Siberia
a servant is a helper or subordinate

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed assistant works on a Russian river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ob is a great Siberian river, a crossword favourite for its short name.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means quick to notice things, so it is a synonym for alert and watchful.
